title: Service Accounts and API Access
summary: Defines how to create service accounts, issue static API keys, configure atomic scopes, and rotate keys on a strict lifecycle.
coverage: Service account creation and login restrictions
Atomic scope model for records and pentests datasets
API key creation, visibility, copy, and rotation workflow
90-day default rotation baseline with optional creation end date

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Service account API keys are sensitive credentials. Share through a secure channel only and rotate immediately after any suspected exposure.

sections.title: Service account model
paragraphs: Service accounts are API-only identities stored in `allowed_users` with `auth_type=service` and `is_service_account=1`.
Service accounts do not receive interactive passwords and cannot sign in through `/login`. They are intended for machine-to-machine integration only.

rows: Single static API key that is viewable by admins and rotatable on demand.
Create account, create/view/rotate key, and set dataset scopes.

sections.title: Atomic scope model
paragraphs: Service API access is controlled by explicit scopes attached to each service account key. Scope checks are enforced in API-key middleware before route execution.
Grant only the minimum scope set required by the integration.

sections.title: Key lifecycle and rotation
paragraphs: At key creation time, admin can optionally set a custom `end_date`. If omitted, expiry is set to 90 days by default.
The key end date set at creation is immutable; editing privileges does not alter expiry.
Admin can rotate any key at any time from service account details. Rotation generates a new key immediately and invalidates the previous key.
orderedList: Create a service account (or convert local-user creation into service-account mode).
Select one or more scopes and create the API key.
Copy the key to your integration secret store.
Periodically rotate the key, or rotate immediately after suspected leakage.
Verify integration calls after rotation and remove old key references.

sections.title: API authentication and security controls
paragraphs: Service API calls accept credentials through `X-API-Key` or `Authorization: Bearer <key>` headers.
The backend applies fingerprint lookup, constant-time key comparison, expiry checks, and scope enforcement before returning datasets.
All service API responses are JSON and unauthorized requests return generic errors to reduce information disclosure.

rows: API key length bounds and strict header parsing.
